summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with hands-on embedded firmware experience across STM32 Cortex-M4, Arduino/AVR, Raspberry Pi, and NVIDIA Jetson platforms. Writes bare-metal embedded C at the register level, including low-level I2C, timer-triggered ADC, and interrupt-driven UART drivers for real-time distributed electromechanical systems.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating an ADXL345 accelerometer with a Raspberry Pi over I2C and an HC-05 Bluetooth link, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID cursor commands.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots, reading and revising schematics through to hardware bring-up and bench debug.
Implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback control across competition robot platforms.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a PyQt data acquisition GUI for real-time instrument readout and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor (Cortex-M4)
bullets: Programmed Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal embedded C at the register level (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with no HAL abstraction, fitting the full firmware in 3.68 KB Flash and 1.58 KB RAM.

Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversion, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C display driver at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; validated bus timing in Proteus before bring-up.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a distributed electromechanical pick-and-place system: embedded Linux services on NVIDIA Jetson (systemd-managed) driving an Arduino/AVR motion controller over USB serial.

Wrote the microcontroller firmware in embedded C++: two-link inverse kinematics, five-servo PWM actuation, and range-gated contact detection using dual VL53L0X ToF sensors multiplexed over I2C via a TCA9548A.
Debugged 11 hardware and low-level software failures (servo brown-out on simultaneous attach, serial errno-5 disconnect recovery, stale-frame capture) to reach 100% pick reliability across 10 trials.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Streamed target commands from an NVIDIA Jetson running YOLOv8 detection to a microcontroller over UART for real-time servo tracking.
Implemented interrupt-driven UART command parsing, multi-servo PWM control, a manual override path, and VL53L0X ToF ranging over I2C with OLED readout.
